fields.description:
Standardize the CLI write-command argument parsing: retire the hand-rolled manual loop for Python's stdlib argparse, WITHOUT changing observable behavior.

## Context / Problem
Today the CLI parses write-command args with a hand-rolled loop (src/rebar/_commands/claim.py _parse_force/_parse_assignee, and src/rebar/_commands/transition.py _parse_flags) carrying bespoke semantics not reflected in any schema: --assignee ABSENT is a None sentinel (=> ticket.default_assignee fallback) while explicit --assignee "" CLEARS the assignee. This is tech-debt: flags and --help can silently drift from actual behavior.

## Dependency / sequencing
Depends on blusterous-earthly-kitten, which normalizes the force surface (removes `force_close`, makes `transition`'s `--force[=<reason>]` a reason-carrying param matching `claim`, and drops the `--reason`-as-force-note fallback). This is a behavior-preserving MECHANICAL refactor that must preserve the POST-blusterous CLI surface, so it runs AFTER that semantic change to avoid re-encoding a soon-to-change flag and to avoid a conflicting edit on the same parser files.

## Approach
Refactor the CLI write-command parsing onto Python's stdlib argparse. argparse is the chosen default: zero new runtime dependency, portable, and it generates accurate --help; we do NOT adopt Click or Typer, to avoid adding a runtime dependency. This is a behavior-preserving ADAPTER REFACTOR, orthogonal to the parity oracle. Respect the module-size (<=800 LOC) and per-function complexity ratchets by extracting along existing call-graph seams rather than inflating a single function.

### Behavioral fidelity (argparse defaults that MUST be overridden)
The hand-rolled loops carry load-bearing behaviors argparse does NOT reproduce by default; the refactor MUST preserve each explicitly:
- **Unknown/extra tokens are silently skipped.** transition._parse_flags ignores tokens it does not recognize. Use `ArgumentParser(add_help=False)` + `parse_known_args()` (NOT `parse_args()`, which errors exit-2 on unrecognized arguments), discarding the extras, to keep the silent-skip semantics.
- **The retired `--force-close` spelling keeps its dedicated exit-1 rejection.** transition recognizes-and-rejects `--force-close`/`--force-close=<x>` with a bespoke message (see test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py). argparse would silently skip it under parse_known_args, so re-add an explicit pre/post-parse rejection raising CommandError(returncode=1) with the existing message + rename guidance.
- **Value-less-flag and invalid-arg errors exit 1 with the current messages**, not argparse's default exit-2 + auto-usage. Construct the parser with `exit_on_error=False` and/or catch `SystemExit`/`argparse.ArgumentError` and re-raise as `CommandError(returncode=1)` carrying the existing message text.

## Contract preservation (must not regress, relative to the post-blusterous surface)
Flag spellings, exit-code 10 (ConcurrencyError), exit-code 1 (validation/retired-flag/value-less-flag), the `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying bypass (bare `--force` -> "(no reason given)"; `--force=<reason>` -> that reason; `--reason` is NOT the force note), the retired `--force-close` exit-1 rejection, silent-skip of unknown tokens, and the --assignee None-vs-empty-string distinction must be preserved exactly.

## Preserving direct callers of the private parse helpers
`transition._parse_flags` is imported and called directly (unpacking its exact 5-tuple `(reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref)` and pinning None-vs-'' + the retired-flag rejection) by three tests OUTSIDE src/rebar/_commands/:
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_ref_target_80af.py (test_parse_flags_reads_ref)
- tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py (None-vs-'' + `--force-close` rejection)
- tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py
To keep these interface/unit tests passing UNCHANGED, `_parse_flags` is RETAINED as a thin argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple with identical semantics (it parses via the new argparse parser internally). claim.py's `_parse_force`/`_parse_assignee` have no external direct callers (grep-verified), so they may be inlined/replaced freely as long as the CLI-observable behavior is preserved.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/claim.py — replace the _parse_force/_parse_assignee hand loop with an argparse-backed parser, preserving the --assignee None-vs-"" sentinel semantics; no external direct callers to preserve.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition.py — replace _parse_flags' hand loop with an argparse-backed parser, but RETAIN `_parse_flags` as a shim returning the same 5-tuple for its three external direct-caller tests.
- Lib and MCP surfaces are OUT OF SCOPE (this is an adapter-local change).

## Testing
- The existing CLI interface tests pass unchanged (tests/interfaces), INCLUDING test_close_ref_target_80af.py's direct `_parse_flags` call (preserved via the shim).
- The existing direct-caller unit/script tests pass unchanged: tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py (None-vs-'' + retired `--force-close` rejection) and tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py.
- `--force[=<reason>]` supplies the audit note inline (bare -> "(no reason given)"); `--reason` is admitted only as close_reason, never as the force note (test, consistent with blusterous).
- --assignee absent => default_assignee fallback; --assignee "" => cleared (test asserts both).
- Unknown/extra tokens are silently skipped (parse_known_args), the retired `--force-close` spelling still exits 1 with its message, and a value-less flag exits 1 (not argparse's exit-2) — behavioral-fidelity tests.
- A ConcurrencyError still exits 10.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI write-command parsing goes through argparse and `--help` is generated (verified by running the command's --help and confirming it lists the flags).
- [ ] The `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying form is preserved (bare -> "(no reason given)", `--force=<reason>` -> that reason); `--reason` is not repurposed as the force note (test).
- [ ] The --assignee None-vs-empty-string distinction is preserved: absent => default_assignee fallback, "" => cleared (test asserts both).
- [ ] `transition._parse_flags` is retained as an argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple, so its three external direct callers (test_close_ref_target_80af.py, test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py, test_dependency_audit.py) pass unchanged.
- [ ] argparse behavioral fidelity is preserved: unknown/extra tokens are silently skipped (parse_known_args, not parse_args), the retired `--force-close` spelling keeps its explicit exit-1 rejection, and value-less/invalid-flag errors exit 1 with the existing messages rather than argparse's default exit-2 + usage.
- [ ] Exit code 10 on ConcurrencyError is preserved (existing CLI interface tests pass).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green; module-size and complexity ratchets respected.
